The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus, leading to an increase in cases where 5G was installed, is a conspiracy theory with no scientific basis. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] Numerous scientific and governmental organizations have debunked this claim. [2] [6] [3] [4] [5]

The International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a UN agency, confirmed in April 2020 that 5G is not responsible for the spread of COVID-19, calling it a "hoax that has no technical basis." [2] [5] The World Health Organization (WHO) and the UK government have also stated that viruses cannot travel via radio waves or mobile networks, and that COVID-19 has spread in countries without 5G. [6] [4]

Experts explain that 5G technology uses electromagnetic fields, and it is physically impossible for these fields to transfer particles like viruses. [6] [7] There is also no scientific evidence to support the idea that 5G compromises the immune system. [6] Despite the lack of evidence, these conspiracy theories led to arson attacks on 5G towers and harassment of telecom engineers in several countries. [1] [6] [3] [8]
